newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris, Armenians in fresh border clashes.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, Armenians in fresh border clashes.

text.p: Armenian and Azeri troops clashed on Sunday near the disputed enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh, Interfax news agency said.

Quoting a military source in the Azeri capital Baku, it said Armenian troops had shelled Azeri positions in the Kazakh and Tauz districts in the northern part of the border and also in the Agdzhabedi district east of Nagorno-Karabakh.
The source said 50 people had died or been wounded in such clashes over the last two days, adding that Armenia's losses were "several times higher than Azerbaijan's".
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
On Saturday the two Caucasian foes accused each other of shelling border villages.

The latest clashes, lasting for over a week, have been the worst since a 1994 cease-fire halted fighting over Nagorno-Karabakh, a predominantly Armenian-populated region which broke away from Azerbaijan in the late 1980s. Thousands of people had died in years of fighting.
More than 20 percent of Azerbaijan's territory, including Karabakh, is now controlled by separatist forces. Baku says this amounts to occupation of its territory by Armenia proper.

Armenia says it was not a formal party in the conflict between Azerbaijan and Karabakh, but it gave its ethnic kin strong moral and military support and Karabakh leader Robert Kocharyan is now the Armenian prime minister.
On Friday Armenia's President Levon Ter-Petrosyan and Azeri leader Haydar Aliyev held a telephone conversation in which they expressed concern over the new fighting, Interfax said.
Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to the ceasefire and ordered their troops to "obey it very strictly", it said.
